mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the Federal Funds rate above 1.5% for three consecutive months reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 1.5% and remains above for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are not statistically lower than during the 12 months prior to the rate hike (t-test p > 0.05) in at least 70% of such regimes.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which raises investor confidence and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by > 10,000 jobs month-over-month while UNRATE decreases by > 0.2 percentage points in the same month
failure_condition: In 40% or more of such labor market strengthening events, the 20-day forward return is negative or flat (Rank IC < 0.5).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in industrial production (INDPRO) exceeding 2% for two consecutive months indicates accelerating economic demand, which anticipates higher corporate profits and supports positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: Over 50 such months, the 5-day forward return is not statistically positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 2% for three consecutive months suggests the Federal Reserve may maintain current policy, reducing policy uncertainty and allowing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL falls below 2% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: In > 60% of such low-inflation periods, the 20-day forward return is non-positive (Rank IC > 0.7).

mechanism_narrative: When the monthly ratio of residential mortgage applications (HOUST) falls by more than 15% in a single month, it indicates cooling housing demand, which typically precedes a tightening in credit conditions and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: In 40% of such events, the 60-day forward return is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in job openings (not directly observable in the provided catalog but as a placeholder for a missing labor proxy) and a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) creates a labor market imbalance that drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls by > 0.3 percentage points while labor market momentum indicators (not in catalog) show expansion
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is not positive in 50% of such events (Rank IC < 0.5).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in consumer inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 4% for four consecutive months suggests the Fed is likely to hold rates steady, reducing risk premiums and producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
failure_condition: Over 80% of such periods, the 5-day forward return is flat or negative (Rank IC > 0.8).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 5% in a month signals supply-side weakness that can erode corporate earnings expectations and drive negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO decreases by > 5% in a single month
failure_condition: In 70% of such contractions, the 20-day forward return is not statistically negative (t-test p > 0.05).
